messages:
alejandro: Heads up — Peregrine (dedicated, us-east-1) reporting a sudden TPS surge (~3.2k tps). Customers seeing 429s + p95 latency spikes to 500-800ms. Billing UI shows burst credits not exhausted. Opening triage.

marta: Confirmed. Pool: dedicated-peregrine-prod. Admission drops starting 12:04 UTC. Incoming ~3200 tps, token_per_second configured ~1000. Autoscale didn't catch up — no warm nodes. Also seeing auth validation latency bump (60-120ms) for some requests.

jules: Possible noisy neighbor or admission headroom calc glitch. Can someone grab the admission snapshot + burst ledger for 12:00-12:08?

jen: @marta can you paste the controller snapshot & any relevant logs? I want to see if the ledger balance was read by the admission controller at the time.

marta: Pasting quick excerpts:
```
$ curl -s "https://admin-api.internal/pools/dedicated-peregrine-prod/admission/snapshot?from=1700000000&to=1700000500"
# snapshot shows: incoming_tps=3200, configured_tps=1000, burst_credit_balance=42,000
# admission decision: throttled_when_window_estimate > headroom
```
Also HPA status: `replicas: 3 -> 8` (scale started at 12:05:13 UTC).

autoscale-bot: Autoscaler event: pool=dedicated-peregrine-prod scale_up triggered at 12:05:13 UTC (3 -> 8). Prewarm not kicked: prewarm threshold "prewarm_token_rate" not met.

jules: Interesting — ledger shows credits available but admission still throttled. Two hypotheses: 1) admission controller cache stale vs ledger (cache TTL 30s), 2) headroom calculation uses 1s lookahead that underestimates incoming burst shape. Also I see GPU host-level saturation on two nodes (high steal/latency) coincident with spike -> noisy tenant possible.

alejandro: Reaching out to Peregrine with quick mitigation: ask them to shift to fallback model variant (lower tokens/s) or reduce concurrency by ~30% for 10m while we stabilize. Also ask for a sample request-id + X-Client-Id header so we can correlate.

marta: I ran a local repro (k6) against the pool to simulate the burst. Repro notes: when synthetic tps crosses configured headroom *and* ledger read lag > 10s, admission rejects even if balance is positive. Root cause looks like a race between ledger refresh and headroom window. Quick patch: bump ledger cache TTL to 60s -> but that may make us more conservative. Better short-term is increasing headroom multiplier to 1.5 and extending lookahead to 15s.

jules: Applied emergency mitigation: headroom multiplier -> 1.5, admission lookahead -> 15s for dedicated-peregrine-prod, enabled emergency-burst-unlock flag (10m). Monitoring: 429s dropped to near-zero in ~45s, p95 latency back under 300ms.

autoscale-bot: Observed: request 429-rate drop from 8.9% -> 0.2% within 60s after emergency settings.

alejandro: Customer reports improvement and accepts temporary fallback for 20m. Filing follow-up infra ticket: REQ-3512 (investigate ledger-read race & prewarm gating conditions). cc @jen @jules. :thumbsup:

jen: Next steps: 1) reproduce ledger-read race with tighter instrumentation, 2) audit prewarm gating logic (why threshold didn't trigger), 3) long-term: add admission path to read ledger snapshot fallback from DB if cache stale > Xs. I'll own the prewarm audit.

marta: Adding metrics + traces to repro: will attach span IDs to the ticket. Leaving emergency settings in place for 15m then revert if autoscale + prewarm confirmed.

jules: Also recommend we add a temporary routing policy to spill new traffic to hosted-fallback for this account in future incidents.

alejandro: Thanks team — I'll keep the customer updated and close once infra ticket has a plan.
